summary.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for the first time (10% margin, up 27% YoY), driven by export price realisations.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 29% YoY, led by cables and wire exports, with PAT of about INR64 crore (up 22% YoY). Management attributed the EBITDA per ton jump to war-risk and volatility premiums on exports, mainly to MENA, rather than volume growth. Bhiwadi XLPE plant (48,000 MT) was commissioned in April 2026 but is running at only 20-25% utilisation, pulling overall utilisation to about 66%. Management reiterated FY27 volume growth of about 15% and a INR5,000 crore top-line ambition by FY30, while flagging that the BESS entry may slip by a couple of quarters.

financial_highlights.change: Up in absolute terms YoY; margin % down as realisations rose

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR300-plus crore in the quarter, mainly MENA
financial_highlights.change: Volume growth in exports only single-digit %
Q1 volume growth about 1% YoY (per analyst)

financial_highlights.value: Rose in Q1; management expects 55-60 days

segments.name: Cables and wire (export)
segments.commentary: Main growth driver; export revenue close to INR300-plus crore in Q1, largely MENA, with better pricing versus Middle East competitors. Volume growth in exports only single-digit %.

segments.name: XLPE compounds
segments.commentary: Installed XLPE capacity raised to 2,14,500 MT after 48,000 MT Bhiwadi greenfield plant (April 2026); company holds more than one-third XLPE compound market share.

segments.name: HFFR compounds
segments.commentary: Capacity expansion targeted to 20,000 MT for FY27; company claims leading presence in India.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: Initial phase of about 1 GWh, supply-led, with capex and working capital of INR150-200 crore, funded from internal accruals; EBITDA margin guided at 6-8% initially. Location shifting West to East, which may delay by a couple of quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of 2,31,000 MT, implying about 60,000 MT per quarter for the remaining quarters; FY27 volume growth guided at about 15%.
FY27 revenue growth guidance about 13-14%, built on prior-year average realisation of about INR145 per kg with no price increase assumed.
Management says it will surpass the conservative annual guidance given the strong Q1, but visibility is only about one to two months given spot order books.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 10-12% (INR16-17 per ton); BESS long-term margin target 11-15%.
Top-line ambition of INR5,000 crore by FY30 reiterated.
Committed FY27 investment INR150-175 crore across Eastern MV capacity, HFFR and Vapi site, plus BESS.
Resin prices expected to take 3-6 months to normalise once the war and Hormuz situation clears.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 3,16,400 MT per annum as of June 2026; management referenced about 3,34,400 MT by year-end (FY27), with about 48,000 MT XLPE and about 25,000 MT PVC added.

Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) greenfield XLPE plant of 48,000 MT commissioned April 2026; running at about 20-25%, with management assuming about 50% average utilisation for FY27 and about INR500 crore potential revenue at full run-rate.
Eastern medium-voltage capability being built; investment already committed, expected operational by end FY27 or Q1 FY28.
New site near Vapi to consolidate products; capex to be incurred.
BESS first phase about 1 GWh, mid-FY29 timeline cited for 1 GW scale; location shifting from West to East (West Bengal being considered), with state incentive policy awaited by end August.
Capex of about INR77 crore already incurred in Q1 (per analyst question, not confirmed in detail).
demand_pricing: Export demand strong early in the war as MENA and US buyers built safety stocks; pricing supported by war-risk and volatility premiums on quotes.
Realisations rose about 30% YoY per management; pass-through model for most customers.
Domestic volumes weak in Q1 due to high prices; management expects volume pickup as price uncertainty subsides.
Bhiwadi capacity aimed at Rajasthan and Delhi domestic customers, with some West capacity redirected to Europe and indirectly the US; new capacity to serve existing customers.
Management says there is no antidumping or BIS requirement on XLPE, HFFR or PVC compounds at present. India-EU FTA expected to benefit European exports.
Company says competitive edge from supply reliability during global disruptions; imports face logistics risk.
Cable customers (T&D) growing about 12-13% per management, with the company targeting 2-3 points above that via share gains.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q1 revenue was carried over from Q4 shipments?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 1,000 MT of export shipments slipped from late March; value rose due to higher freight. Some of the INR300-plus crore export revenue came from prior-quarter quantities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pricing benefited from freight and raw material volatility, adding roughly INR2.5-3 per ton. Management says INR19.6 per ton is unlikely to sustain each quarter, versus a normal INR15-17 range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Starts as supply plus EPC with 6-8% EBITDA margin; system integrator and backward integration could add 2-3 points per stage, with long-term 11-15%. BOO/BOOT not planned for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth split between volume and realisation in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance assumes no price increase versus last year's INR145-odd average realisation; volume growth is about 15% and is the key metric to track.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bhiwadi running at only 20-25%?
qa_highlights.answer: The plant commissioned in April 2026 and is ramping up; management expects about 50% average utilisation for FY27, with contribution rising in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share given raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Bhiwadi aims to take share in Indian medium-voltage XLPE; it sees import substitution opportunity given supply chain disruption, though it will serve existing customers only.

risks_watch: Sustainability of export pricing premiums; July prices eased slightly and management says Q2 export revenue may be below the INR300 crore level.
Bhiwadi ramp-up pace (20-25% now versus 50% assumed) and whether H2 operating leverage materialises.
Finance costs rose on working capital build; management expects them to ease from July.
BESS timeline risk: relocation to East may delay by a couple of quarters; retendering of low-priced bids; West Bengal incentive policy pending.
Geopolitical risk (Hormuz, Middle East) and possible crude price increase affecting demand and project costs.
Cash conversion cycle expected to normalise to 55-60 days from elevated Q1 levels.
key_quotes: So it is very difficult to predict on this line.
maybe INR19.6 something which has been achieved in this quarter may not be sustainable for each and every quarter, but probably it can be sustainable for a few months from here also.
We are conservative in our approach.
So it is very difficult to comment that how long this type of export business will continue month-on-month basis.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the structural demand story, long-term capacity plans and the FY27 volume target, but cautious on near-term visibility. Management repeatedly declined to forecast beyond about one to two months, citing spot order books, Hormuz uncertainty and volatile resin prices, and conceded that Q1 export pricing and EBITDA per ton are not repeatable every quarter.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 13-14% and volume growth of about 15% (2,31,000 MT target), backed by the 48,000 MT Bhiwadi XLPE plant, but Q1 volume grew only about 1% YoY, the new plant runs at 20-25%, and the Q1 jump was price-driven and may not persist.
